module_title: NEP 2020 & NCF-SE 2023: The New Architectural Framework
introduction: This foundational level introduces the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and its curricular counterpart, the National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) 2023. It maps the historic shift from the 10+2 system to the 5+3+3+4 design and establishes the core vision of holistic, competency-based education.

core_concepts.title: NEP 2020: Background and Vision
core_concepts.description:
Approved on July 29, 2020, NEP 2020 replaced the 34-year-old NPE 1986. 
- Committee Chair: Dr. K. Kasturirangan (Former ISRO Chief).
- Structural Change: Renamed the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) back to the **Ministry of Education (MoE)**.
- Core Vision: To transform India into a vibrant knowledge society by making education more holistic, flexible, multidisciplinary, and aligned with 21st-century skills.

core_concepts.title: The 5+3+3+4 Curricular Structure
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 completely dismantles the old 10+2 structure, replacing it with a cognitive-developmental model covering ages 3 to 18:
1. Foundational Stage (5 Years / Ages 3-8): 3 years of Anganwadi/Preschool (Balvatika) + Classes 1 & 2. Focus: Play-based, activity-based learning. No exams.
2. Preparatory Stage (3 Years / Ages 8-11): Classes 3 to 5. Focus: Discovery, interactive classroom learning, and introduction to light textbooks.
3. Middle Stage (3 Years / Ages 11-14): Classes 6 to 8. Focus: Experiential learning in sciences, mathematics, arts, and humanities. Introduction of vocational crafts.
4. Secondary Stage (4 Years / Ages 14-18): Classes 9 to 12. Focus: Multidisciplinary study, critical thinking, flexibility, and student choice of subjects (No hard separation between Arts, Commerce, and Science).

core_concepts.title: Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE)
core_concepts.description: NEP 2020 recognizes that over 85% of cumulative brain development occurs prior to age 6. For the first time, ECCE (Ages 3-6) is formally brought into the mainstream school system structure to ensure school readiness via Anganwadis and Balvatikas.

core_concepts.title: National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCF-SE) 2023
core_concepts.description: NCF-SE 2023 is the document that operationalizes the vision of NEP 2020 in the classroom. It shifts the focus entirely from rote memorization to **Competency-Based Education (CBE)**. The curriculum focuses on 'learning how to learn' (Metacognition) rather than just memorizing facts.

important_entities.name: NIPUN Bharat Mission
important_entities.key_fact: National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy.
important_entities.significance: A direct outcome of NEP 2020. The policy stated that the highest priority is achieving Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) by Grade 3. NIPUN Bharat aims to ensure every child in India achieves FLN by Grade 3 by the year 2026-27.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often forget that the new 5+3+3+4 system explicitly includes 3 years of pre-schooling. The old 10+2 system only covered ages 6 to 18. The new system covers ages **3 to 18**. Examiners will test if you know the entry age is now 3 years, not 6.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: F P M S (Foundational, Preparatory, Middle, Secondary)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember FPMS to get the stages in chronological order. First you lay the **F**oundation, then you **P**repare, then hit the **M**iddle, and finally finish at **S**econdary.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks which stage introduces 'Vocational Education' and internships (bagless days), the answer is always the **Middle Stage (Grade 6)**.
